description: The course has two parts: synthesis and filters. In the synthesis part, students learn to obtain a network from a given network function. In the filter part, students learn the basic concepts and design of constant K, m-derived and active filters. They also use these concepts to solve some real-world engineering problems.

syllabus.title: Fundamental Concepts
syllabus.body: Network functions, positive real functions, Hurwitz polynomials, basic synthesis technique.

syllabus.title: One-Port and Two-Port Synthesis
syllabus.body: Synthesis of one-port network functions with two kinds of elements - Foster and Cauer forms for LC, RC and RL immittance functions. Certain RLC function realizations. Fundamentals of two-port synthesis.

syllabus.title: Passive Filters
syllabus.body: Analysis and design of constant k and m-derived low pass, high pass, band pass and band stop filters.

syllabus.title: Active Filters
syllabus.body: Theory of active filters, filter function definitions and specifications, the realization of active low pass and high pass filters. Maximally flat filters. Cascading of filters - Butterworth and Chebyshev filters. Frequency transformations. Case study and simulations.

outcomes: Determine whether a given driving function can be synthesized or not.
Obtain one / two-port networks from a given network function.
Understand and design different passive filters.
Understand and design active filters and implement the course contents in real-life problems.

referenceBooks: F. F. Kuo, Network Analysis and Synthesis, Wiley International Edition, 2008.
Steve Winder, Analog and Digital Filter Design, 2nd Edition, Newnes, Elsevier Science, 2002.
